engine_step_at_issue: Colorado sales tax refund: the engine computed $19 from modified AGI of $4,625.40 using the TY2025 refund table (single, $52,000 or less, $19), as if a TABOR refund were owed for TY2026.
summary: The law gives $0 in Colorado refundable credits for this filer in 2026. The head is 66 and childless, so there is no federal EITC and therefore no Colorado EITC. There is also no CTC, FATC or child care credit, and the Senior Housing Credit was not extended. The TABOR sales tax refund under C.R.S. 39-22-2003 is paid only when there is excess revenue in the fiscal year ending in the tax year (FY 2025-26), and the pre-freeze forecasts project revenue below the Referendum C cap with no income-tax-form refunds. The engine's $19 is exactly the TY2025 DR 0104 single-filer amount for modified AGI of $52,000 or less, carried into 2026 when no 2026 refund was owed or published.
